## The Compliance Gap Is Wider Than You Think

Most local governments have hundreds of untagged PDFs on their websites. The federal deadline is approaching fast.

### DOJ Enforcement Is Real

The Department of Justice finalized ADA Title II digital accessibility rules in April 2024. Compliance deadlines are April 24, 2026 for populations of 50,000+ and April 26, 2027 for smaller municipalities.

### Compliance Is More Than PDFs

ADA Title II requires WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for all web content — web pages, PDFs, videos, audio, and documents. Most governments are only thinking about PDFs when the rule covers everything on their website.

### No Single Tool Covers It All

Governments are cobbling together WCAG scanners, PDF remediators, and spreadsheets. Without a unified system, there's no defensible audit trail and no way to prove compliance to the DOJ.

A11y Audit — ADA Title II & WCAG 2.2 AA Compliance Platform

# Accessibility Compliance You Can Prove

Public agencies use A11y Audit to meet ADA Title II and Section 508: crawl every page and document, run the automated checks, work through the manual review no tool can judge, and walk away with signed evidence that holds up. Private teams use the same platform to reach WCAG 2.2 Level AA.

## For public agencies, the rule is already in force

The Department of Justice's ADA Title II rule sets WCAG 2.1 Level AA as the standard for state and local government websites and mobile apps. If your entity serves 50,000 people or more, that requirement took effect on April 24, 2026 — it applies to you today. Entities under 50,000 and special district governments have until April 26, 2027.

A11y Audit holds your content to WCAG 2.2 Level AA — a newer, stricter standard than the rule's floor — so meeting it keeps you ahead of the requirement rather than level with it. Your web pages, your PDFs, and your mobile apps are all in scope, and A11y Audit covers all three.

## A platform, not a spot-check

Your team logs in and works the whole job in one place — discovery, scanning, manual review, remediation, and the evidence at the end.
